correctness.rationale: Eight disjoint run-shape candidates are derived by exhausting zero-only, one-only, repeated mixed transitions, two possible three-run orientations and all longer factors. The proof handles collisions with unique pure-zero factors and unit differences of one-run lengths, and establishes a necessary length lower bound 10 with a matching parameter family. An occurrence-table checker verifies complete MUS sets for 7,776 tuples; an independently designed suffix-neighbor checker verifies 16,807 complete tuples and 180 longer trials; neither is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The five-run binary family provides a natural first interaction of three same-letter runs and competing two-sided bridges. The exact unrestricted factor-template classification removes the non-generic cases explicitly excluded by prior work, tightens the relevant generic nine-factor upper bound to eight, and identifies the first possible eight-factor length 10 rather than length 13 under the old separated assumption. Such output-size and explicit factor identities are meaningful for MUS-based text-indexing and combinatorics; no speculative algorithmic speedup is asserted.
